Then provide tips for the best results (fat content, thawing process, consistency, flavor enhancement).Yes, you can absolutely use frozen milk to make homemade coffee ice cream. Frozen milk is completely safe to use in cooked ice cream bases (like custard) or even uncooked Philadelphia-style bases, as the freezing and thawing processes do not compromise the safety or quality of the milk for this purpose. 

Since you will be melting the milk into your ice cream base or blending it with other ingredients, any slight changes in texture that occur when freezing won't affect the final product.

Here are a few tips to ensure your ice cream turns out perfectly:

*   **Thoroughly Thaw and Mix:** Before adding the milk to your ice cream base, make sure it is completely thawed in the refrigerator. When milk freezes, the water and fats can separate. Shake or whisk the thawed milk vigorously to recombine the components before using it.
*   **Opt for Whole Milk:** For the creamiest texture in your coffee ice cream, use whole milk. If you only have lower-fat milk, you can balance it by adding a bit of heavy cream.
*   **Brewing your Coffee:** Rather than using liquid milk as the sole liquid for infusing coffee flavor, you can also dissolve high-quality instant coffee powder or espresso powder directly into the thawed milk before heating, or steep fresh coffee beans or grounds in the milk. 

**Quick Ice Cream Base Suggestion:**
If you want a simple and delicious recipe, try combining your thawed milk with heavy cream, sugar, and a few tablespoons of espresso powder. Gently heat the mixture just enough to dissolve the sugar and coffee, let it cool completely in the refrigerator, and then churn it in your ice cream maker according to the manufacturer's instructions.
